correctness.rationale: Using the exactly normalized triangular density for differences of independent uniform side-generator coordinates, multinomial expansion gives \(m_1=S/6\), \(m_2=S^2/15-7P/90+Z/9\), and \(m_3=S^3/28-31SP/420+2SZ/15\). The linear system has exact determinant \(-41/18900\), so the first three even distance moments recover \(P=AB\) and \(Z=C^2\). The sum \(S=A+B\) and product \(P\) recover the unordered positive squared lengths, and \(Z\) recovers the absolute dot product. This establishes all congruence cases including repeated lengths and orthogonality. Two explicit positive-definite Gram matrices have equal first two even moments and distinct third moments by \(41/16800\). All coefficients, determinant and examples were recomputed in a standalone exact rational checker; finite random cases are supplementary and do not replace the universal algebraic proof.

value.rationale: The object is the natural first nontrivial three-parameter centrally symmetric polygon, and interpoint distance distributions are a recognized geometric tomography invariant. Recovering all parallelograms from exactly three unlabeled global even-distance moments is a full finite-data inverse theorem in a nongeneric parallel-sided class, contrasted with entire-distribution and directional reconstruction. An explicit collision proves two initial even moments are insufficient, a motivated exact sharp cutoff; no general-polygon or arbitrary-statistics significance is claimed.
